## Knowledge Priming

- Before non-trivial work, read the repository context: the README, the architecture document and the local overlay.
- When repository evidence and general practice disagree, follow the repository. Say so; do not override it in silence.
- An instruction from the user in the current task overrides this file. A path-scoped instruction overrides it for the files it matches.

## Code Is Authoritative

- A code file carries no prose: no comment and no docstring. The code is the only source of truth, so a change cannot leave a stale claim beside it.
- A directive that a tool reads stays: `noqa`, `nosec`, `type: ignore`, `pragma: no cover`, a shebang, `fmt: off`, a licence header.
- Put the fact that a comment would carry where it stays true: a name, a test name, the tracker record or a README. When code needs prose to say what it does, fix the code.
- The `no-comments` hook refuses the commit. This command removes the comments:

```sh
python3 .basicly/core/kit/comments/cli.py fix <path>
```

## Core Rules

- Make the smallest diff that meets the requirement. An unrelated change hides which change failed.
- Build only what the task asks for. A speculative abstraction or an unrequested option is a guess that stays in the code.
- Reuse before you build. Prove that a capability is absent by reading the code that would use it, not the documentation or `--help`.
- Fix the root cause. Check every other call site before you call a fix complete.
- Match the style and the names of the file you edit.
- Leave no dead code and no debug output. Never swallow an error: it becomes a wrong answer.
- Keep tests deterministic. A bug fix ships with a regression test.
- Back every claim with evidence: the file you read, the command you ran, the test that passed.

## Mistake Proofing

Make a wrong use impossible, or stop it at once with the fix (poka-yoke). A refusal in the code acts before the damage. A warning in a document acts after it.

- Refuse a wrong input by name. Never answer it with a default or an empty result, because both read as success. Say what is wrong and give the correct command.
- Make the safe behaviour the default. A mode that can damage shared state needs an explicit flag.
- Keep each rule in one place, and call it from every side. Two copies drift and give two answers.
- When a mistake can happen again, add a gate or a test that refuses it. A note does not stop it.

## Secure Coding

- Validate external input at the trust boundary. Code past the boundary assumes the input is safe.
- Pass shell arguments and query values as parameters. Concatenated input runs as syntax.
- Keep secrets in environment variables or a secret manager, out of the repository and the logs. A commit outlives the fix.
- Log the internal detail and return a generic message. A stack trace or a path maps the system.
- Commit no machine path, user name or host name. It breaks the next clone. The tracker's holder field is the one exception: it records the name you choose with `git config basicly.holder`.

## Decision Protocol

- Decide yourself when the choice rests on code you read, is small, can be undone, and is not on the confirmation list.
- Stop and ask when a fact is missing, when sources conflict, or when an assumption you cannot check would change the result. Name what is missing and the answer that unblocks you. Offer only options you would take.
- When rules conflict, follow the safety and security rule.
- When the same approach fails twice, report the pattern and propose another approach.

## External Facts

- Do not answer from memory about a third-party interface. A flag, field, model id, price, limit or version can change. Read our own adapter first, then the vendor's current documentation. The `interface-facts` skill gives the steps.
- An empty search result does not prove absence. Before you report a zero, run a positive control: a search that must match a case you have seen. When the control is also empty, the search is wrong.
- Derive a number twice, by two paths that share no step. When they disagree, suspect the instrument first.
- When two causes predict the same result, say so and change the probe until they differ.

## Require Explicit Confirmation

Ask the user before you:

- force-push, rewrite history, or discard uncommitted work: `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, `git stash`, `git clean`, `rm -rf`;
- read or write a `.env*` file;
- delete files, branches or data outside the task;
- edit CI/CD, deployment, infrastructure, ignore or secrets files;
- add, remove or upgrade a dependency;
- make a network call outside the task.

The deny-list blocks only some of these, and it differs per agent. A command that runs unblocked still needs confirmation. To undo your own edit, restore the file from a copy you made first.

IMPORTANT: never defeat a gate to make it pass. Do not skip or weaken a test, a lint or a type check, and do not bypass a hook (`--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`). Fix the cause.

## Project Overview

- basicly distributes a harness for coding agents. One YAML catalog is projected into agent instruction files, skills and git hooks. Other repositories install it with `basicly install`.
- Stack: Python 3.14 or later, managed with `uv`. The version lives only in `src/basicly/__init__.py`. Platforms: Linux and macOS, tested in CI; Windows runs but CI no longer tests it.
- The `basicly` CLI is `src/basicly/cli.py`. This repository authors the catalog in `.basicly/core/`; its own overrides are in `.basicly-local/`. Scripts and CI helpers are in `.scripts/`.
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` is the authoritative design reference.
- A change under `.basicly/core/kit/` must work for a consumer with no engine. Name where that consumer gets the capability.

## Harness Loop

- Start a session with `basicly session start`. End it with a note tagged `[session handover <date>]` on the root record.
- The tracker ledger is the source of truth for the work.
- Drive non-trivial work through the harness loop. The `harness-loop` skill describes the phases, the commands and the checkpoints.

## Quality Gate

- Review the diff. Then run the change the way a consumer runs it, and read the output. Passing tests do not prove a working feature.
- Run the repository checks on what you touched, after the last edit. A later edit can break what passed.
- Read the pass or fail summary line. Truncated output hides failures.
- Report only what you ran, and say what you did not run. Do not turn "expected to work" into "works".
- When you claim that a check covers every item, name the list that the code reads. A general mechanism does not prove which items it covers.
- Check a claim against the code before it goes into a plan, a design document, a README or a release note. Mark a part that rests on code you did not read as an assumption.

## Catalog Authoring

- Write catalog sources as YAML, never as a discoverable `.md` file. In a repository that installs basicly, put your sources in `.basicly-local/`, because `basicly install` overwrites `.basicly/core/`.
- Start a source with `basicly catalog new skill` or `basicly catalog new fragment`, and follow the `catalog-authoring` skill. `basicly catalog lint` checks the format.

## Session Completion

- Before you end a session, follow the `session-finish` skill. Leave the repository clean, with no partial edits and no stray files. Report what changed, what you verified and what is still open.
- After a refused change or a mistake the user corrected, name the root cause. Propose the fragment, skill or hook change that would have refused it. A note to "be careful" changes nothing.

## Commands

Run these commands as written.

Setup:

```sh
uv sync --group dev
uv run pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t commit-msg -t pre-push
```

Test, whole suite then one file:

```sh
uv run pytest -q
uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py -q
```

Lint / format:

```sh
uv run ruff check
uv run ruff format --check
```

Projection gates (after editing catalog sources):

```sh
uv run basicly check
uv run basicly skills-check
uv run basicly styles-check
uv run basicly agents-check
uv run basicly hooks-check
uv run basicly permissions-check
```

## Git Discipline

- Run `git commit` as its own command. Do not chain `git push`, a tag or a tracker update after it, because a refused commit leaves the chain half done.
- The `commit-msg` hooks require a Conventional Commits subject and a trailing record id. The `conventional-commits` skill writes the message, and the `work-tracker` skill claims the record first.
- When a hook refuses a commit, fix the cause it names and commit again.

## Non-Interactive Shell

- Prefer a cross-platform command to shell-specific behaviour.
- Pass a non-interactive flag to a command that can wait for an answer: `cp -f`, `mv -f`, `rm -f`, `-y`, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`. Some shells alias these commands to interactive mode.
- Never loop over an unquoted variable (`for x in $LIST`). zsh does not split it, so the loop runs once and looks like success. Use an array (`"${arr[@]}"`), an inline list or one batch command, and check that the count changed.
- Before a scripted replace across many sites, state the expected count, and compare it after. A different count is a stop.

## External Review

Before a research or design document recommends a third-party project:

- Treat its README as a claim. Find the call sites and cite `file:line`. A symbol with no non-test caller does not ship.
- Test an absolute claim by trying to break it. A feature can exist and still be described too strongly.
- Read every licence file first, `NOTICE` included, and check each directory. A licence restricts copying the code, not learning a fact from it.
- Ask what the author sells. A recommended control that is the author's own product needs independent evidence.
- Check whether the argument assumes away a control this repository already runs.
- Say whether you established the mechanism or only a correlation.

## Model Tier Routing

- A dispatch declares a tier: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `maximum`. It never names a provider model id; the tier kit's model map resolves the tier.
- Choose the tier by the cost per landed correct change: tokens, time and human interventions. A weak model's mistakes return as rework on the same change.
- Use `low` only for work whose wrong answer a check catches and a rerun fixes cheaply. Start implementation from prose, decomposition, design and costly judgements at `high`.
- A dispatch with no tier is a bug. It inherits the session's own model.

## Rendered Surfaces

A rendered page is an image. A page can pass every check and still be unreadable, so look at the picture:

- Render the page and open the screenshot before you call it done. On WSL, drive Windows Chrome over a UNC path:

```sh
chrome.exe --headless=new --disable-gpu --window-size=1920,1080 --screenshot=<win-path> "file://\\\\wsl.localhost\\<distro>\\<path>"
```

- Check each acceptance criterion against the picture.
- Render from real data as well as the fixture. A fixture with fewer rows hides an overflow.
- Run the overflow check and read both of its signals, `render-overflow` and `render-overlap`. A clipped box shows no scrollbar.

```sh
uv run python .scripts/check_render_overflow.py <page.html>
```

- Shoot every viewport width the layout claims.

## Release Fragments

- A change a consumer can see writes `changelog.d/<record-id>.<category>.md` before its record closes: one bullet line, under 400 characters.
- Write it in the same change. The release reads the tagged commit, and a closed record with a shipped scope and no fragment blocks the next commit on main.

## Platform-Hermetic Tests

The local gate runs on one OS, and CI runs the others only after the push. So make the platform an input to the test:

- Test a path rule with both `PureWindowsPath` and `PurePosixPath`. `Path` takes the form of the host.
- Compare paths as `Path` objects, or render both sides with the same `as_posix()`.
- Do not use `select` or `selectors` on a pipe, because on Windows they accept only sockets. Read in a thread and bound the read with `join(timeout=...)`.
- Wait for a condition, not a duration. Measure time with a monotonic clock.
- Use `skipif` only when the behaviour cannot exist on the other platform.
